cultural_context.description: Rajasthan has a rich and varied cultural heritage expressed through folk music and dance, fairs and festivals, visual arts and crafts, traditional clothing, cuisine, architecture, and regional languages and dialects.
cultural_context.important_note: Cultural practices vary across regions, communities, religions, families, generations, and individual contexts. Information in this file should not be treated as universal to every person in Rajasthan.

source.organization: Government of Rajasthan
source.title: Heritage and Culture

communication_guidance: Use respectful communication when interacting with local people.
Rajasthan contains multiple regional dialects and languages, so do not assume that one speech form represents the entire state.
When participating in a cultural or religious event, follow the guidance of local hosts, organizers, or the relevant venue.
greetings_and_communication.limitation: The current verified knowledge base does not contain a sufficiently sourced phrase list for everyday greetings. Do not invent Rajasthani phrases or translations.

verified_information.description: Rajasthan Tourism states that cuisine varies across the state and identifies dishes including dal-bati-churma, laal maans, safed maans, soyeta, and lasun-ki-chutney among renowned foods.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of Rajasthan
source.title: Rajasthan at a Glance

verified_information.description: The Government of Rajasthan notes that fairs and festivals commonly feature traditional Rajasthani food alongside traditional attire, folk songs, and folk dance.

source.organization: Government of Rajasthan
source.title: Know Rajasthan

dining_guidance: Do not assume one Rajasthani dish represents the food culture of the entire state.
Regional food preferences and dishes can differ between parts of Rajasthan.
Respect individual dietary choices and follow the guidance of hosts at traditional meals or community events.
food_and_dining.limitation: The verified knowledge base does not establish universal everyday dining etiquette for every region and community in Rajasthan.

core_values.name: Cultural continuity
core_values.description: The Government of Rajasthan describes fairs and festivals as contributing to the preservation of tradition and culture.

source.organization: Government of Rajasthan
source.title: Fairs & Festivals

core_values.name: Hospitality
core_values.description: Official Rajasthan Tourism material describes hospitality as a notable part of Rajasthan's cultural image, while visitors should still avoid assuming that every person or community behaves identically.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of Rajasthan
source.title: Rajasthan at a Glance

festivals.name: Gangaur
festivals.description: Gangaur is a major Rajasthan festival associated with the worship of Gauri or Parvati and Shiva. Rajasthan's official cultural material documents women and girls participating in worship, songs, processions, and related traditions.

source.organization: Government of Rajasthan
source.title: History and Culture of Rajasthan – Celebrations, Festivals, and Fairs

festivals.name: Teej
festivals.description: Rajasthan Tourism describes Teej as a major festival in Rajasthan, particularly associated with women, religious observances, singing, dancing, mehndi, colourful clothing, festive food, and processions in Jaipur.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of Rajasthan
source.title: Experience the Festivities of Rajasthan – The colours of Teej

festivals.name: Pushkar Fair
festivals.period: Usually around October-November; dates vary annually
festivals.description: The Government of Rajasthan lists Pushkar Fair among the state's major fairs and festivals.

source.organization: Government of Rajasthan
source.title: Fairs & Festivals

festivals.name: Desert Festival
festivals.period: Usually in January-February; dates vary annually
festivals.description: The Government of Rajasthan lists the Desert Festival in Jaisalmer among the state's major festivals.

source.organization: Government of Rajasthan
source.title: Fairs & Festivals

festivals.name: Marwar Festival
festivals.period: Ashwin, generally September-October; dates vary annually
festivals.description: Rajasthan Tourism describes the Marwar Festival in Jodhpur as a two-day festival featuring folk music and dance associated with the Marwar region and celebrations remembering the heroes of Rajasthan.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of Rajasthan
source.title: Marwar Festival

traditional_dances.name: Ghoomar
traditional_dances.description: Ghoomar is a recognized Rajasthani dance tradition and is identified by the Rajasthan Foundation among the state's notable dance styles.

source.organization: Government of Rajasthan
source.title: Heritage and Culture

traditional_dances.name: Kalbeliya
traditional_dances.description: Kalbeliya is a recognized Rajasthani dance style and is identified by the Rajasthan Foundation among the state's notable dance traditions.

source.organization: Government of Rajasthan
source.title: Heritage and Culture

traditional_dances.name: Gair
traditional_dances.description: Gair is documented by Rajasthan Tourism as a folk dance performed during the Mount Abu Summer Festival.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of Rajasthan
source.title: Summer Festival – Mount Abu

traditional_dances.name: Daph
traditional_dances.description: Daph is documented by Rajasthan Tourism among the folk dance styles presented during the Mount Abu Summer Festival.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of Rajasthan
source.title: Summer Festival – Mount Abu

traditional_clothing.name: Traditional Rajasthani attire
traditional_clothing.description: Official Rajasthan Tourism material describes colourful traditional clothing, including women's long colourful skirts and odhnis and men's kurtas and turbans. Clothing varies by region, community, occasion, and individual.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of Rajasthan
source.title: People of Rajasthan

traditional_arts.name: Folk music
traditional_arts.description: The Rajasthan Foundation identifies folk music as an important part of Rajasthani culture and notes its connection with everyday life and the desert environment.

source.organization: Government of Rajasthan
source.title: Heritage and Culture

traditional_arts.name: Traditional artwork and crafts
traditional_arts.description: The Rajasthan Foundation documents colourful artwork, block prints, intricate furniture carving, textiles, semi-precious stones, and handicrafts as parts of Rajasthan's cultural heritage.

source.organization: Government of Rajasthan
source.title: Heritage and Culture

traditional_arts.name: Puppetry
traditional_arts.description: Rajasthan Tourism documents puppetry shows as part of cultural programming, including at the Kumbhalgarh Festival.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of Rajasthan
source.title: Kumbhalgarh Festival

spiritual_and_cultural_practices.name: Festival rituals
spiritual_and_cultural_practices.description: Rajasthan Tourism documents a range of rites and rituals associated with important life events and festivals, including naming ceremonies, wedding rituals, and festival worship. These practices should be understood in their specific cultural and community contexts.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of Rajasthan
source.title: Customs and Rituals

spiritual_and_cultural_practices.name: Music and devotional traditions
spiritual_and_cultural_practices.description: Rajasthan Tourism notes that folk music and dance vary by region and that many traditional songs have religious or devotional associations.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of Rajasthan
source.title: Customs and Rituals

visitor_guidance: Treat local customs, religious practices, festivals, folk performances, and community celebrations with respect.
Do not assume a practice documented for one region or festival applies throughout Rajasthan.
Ask before photographing people or culturally significant activities when permission or local rules are unclear.
Respect traditional clothing, crafts, music, and dance as cultural heritage rather than treating them only as tourist entertainment.
Rajasthan has substantial regional variation in dialect, cuisine, dress, and cultural practices; avoid presenting one regional tradition as universal.
When attending a religious or cultural event, follow the guidance of local hosts, organizers, or venue authorities.
knowledge_limitations: The verified knowledge base does not provide a sufficiently sourced everyday Rajasthani phrasebook.
The verified knowledge base does not establish universal everyday dining etiquette for all regions and communities.
The verified knowledge base does not provide verified rental prices or specific housing recommendations for Rajasthan.
The verified knowledge base does not provide a comprehensive state-wide transportation etiquette guide.
Traditional clothing varies by region, community, gender, occasion, and individual; descriptions should not be converted into universal dress rules.
Festival dates vary from year to year according to calendars and local schedules; current dates should be checked against official festival information.
Customs and rituals described by official tourism sources may relate to particular communities or life events and should not be presented as practices followed by every Rajasthani person.
ai_response_rules: Use this knowledge base as the primary factual source for Rajasthan-specific cultural claims.
Do not invent Rajasthani phrases or translations.
Use the festival information for festival-specific guidance and do not turn a local or community-specific practice into a universal Rajasthan-wide rule.
Use traditional_dances, traditional_clothing, traditional_arts, and spiritual_and_cultural_practices to explain documented heritage and customs.
Do not invent food customs, rental prices, housing recommendations, transportation rules, or religious practices that are not supported by this knowledge base.
Clearly state when a practice varies by region, community, religion, family, generation, or locality.
If the knowledge base does not contain enough verified information about a topic, say so rather than guessing.
Personalize the guide using verified information, but do not introduce unsupported Rajasthan-specific factual claims.
